standard.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
standard.note: ASVS 4.0.3 is used because its requirement numbers are stable and well known. Controls here group related ASVS requirements; the asvs field lists the requirement ids each control answers. Self-assessed, no third party has reviewed it.

statuses.enforced: Core enforces it in code or CI and a named test or CI job proves it.
statuses.partial: Core enforces part of it, or enforces it only when the edition wires it in; the note says what is missing.
statuses.not-applicable-to-Core: Core has no such surface (it is a library and an API module, not an application with pages, sessions or users).
statuses.edition-responsibility: The edition (RivetIT, RivetMSP) must implement it; Core gives a tested helper or a rule where it can. Listed in docs/design/security-baseline-edition-prompts.md.
statuses.gap: Not done. Nothing enforces it today.

controls.title: Threat model
controls.requirement: A threat model exists and is kept current for the components.
controls.how: docs/security/threat-model.md (assets, trust boundaries, STRIDE per module). No automated check that it is current.
controls.note: Reviewed in the 2026-10 audit; freshness is a manual duty.

controls.title: Documented security review and remediation
controls.requirement: Security findings are tracked to a fix with regression tests.
controls.how: docs/security/CORE_SECURITY_AUDIT.md and CORE_REMEDIATION.md list each finding with its fix commit and a regression test that fails without the fix.
controls.note: Open items are listed as gaps below (GAP-03, GAP-04, GAP-05).

controls.title: Core has no direct database or request-global coupling
controls.requirement: Trusted-layer separation: Core talks to storage only through interfaces and never reads request globals.
controls.how: CI step 'Core must not reference mysqli or request globals' and the PDO-containment step fail the build on a violation.

controls.title: Public API compatibility is checked
controls.requirement: Interfaces between components are controlled and changes are reviewed.
controls.how: docs/api-surface.md is regenerated from the code and a unit test fails when it drifts; a BC check guards public signatures.

controls.title: Minimum password length 12, long passwords accepted
controls.requirement: Passwords of at least 12 characters, up to 64 or more accepted, no composition rules.
controls.how: Core has no user accounts. SecurityBaseline::passwordLengthOk() and the locked floor (MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12) give editions one tested rule to call.
controls.note: The edition must call it on every password set.

controls.title: Password storage uses a slow salted hash
controls.requirement: Passwords are stored with Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2.
controls.how: Core stores no user passwords. Device and panel credentials are 256-bit random tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes (see AUTH-04).
controls.note: Editions use password_hash() in their own user store.

controls.title: Breached-password check
controls.requirement: Passwords are checked against a breached-password list.
controls.how: Nothing in Core or its helper does this.
controls.note: Edition feature; see GAP-06.

controls.title: Service and device credentials are random, hashed at rest, compared in constant time
controls.requirement: Service credentials are high entropy, not stored in plaintext, and compared safely.
controls.how: DeviceRepository and PanelAuthenticator look a bearer token up by its SHA-256 and compare with hash_equals; enrollment issues the credential once and stores only its hash.

controls.title: Credential kinds cannot be swapped; revocation is immediate
controls.requirement: A panel token never works on an agent endpoint and a revoked device is refused at once.
controls.how: Device kind is checked at authentication; revocation clears the credential.

controls.title: Anti-automation on enrollment and MCP
controls.requirement: Throttling against credential guessing and abuse.
controls.how: Enrollment attempts are recorded and locked per selector; MCP calls are rate limited through the Redis limiter; Redis fails open by design.
controls.note: INFO-04: no per-IP throttle on failed device credentials (256-bit tokens make guessing infeasible). Interactive-login throttling is the edition's.

controls.title: Multi-factor authentication available and required for administrators
controls.requirement: MFA is available, and required for administrative access.
controls.how: Core has no interactive login. SecurityBaseline::mfaRequired() fixes the rule (always for administrators, on by default for others, opt-out per client audit-logged through BaselineChanges).
controls.note: The edition must implement TOTP/WebAuthn and call the rule.

controls.title: Recovery and out-of-band flows
controls.requirement: Secure password recovery, no default accounts, out-of-band verifiers.
controls.how: No recovery or out-of-band flow exists in Core.

controls.title: No default credentials or secrets in the repository
controls.requirement: No default passwords; secrets are not in source.
controls.how: scripts/secret-scan.php scans the tree and history with an allowlist that needs a written reason per fixture; CI runs it plus gitleaks. No default account or default password ships in Core.

controls.title: Session cookies are Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, __Host-
controls.requirement: Cookie-based sessions carry Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and the __Host- prefix.
controls.how: Core sets no cookies. SecurityBaseline::cookieAttributes() always returns Secure and HttpOnly true and never SameSite=None; hostCookieName() gives the prefix.
controls.note: Locked settings cookie_secure and cookie_httponly.

controls.title: Idle timeout default 30 minutes, ceiling 8 hours
controls.requirement: Sessions expire; users can log out; re-authentication for sensitive actions.
controls.how: SecurityBaseline defines session_idle_minutes (default 30, max 480); the edition applies it.

controls.title: Session identifiers, token-based sessions
controls.requirement: New session on login, high-entropy ids, no URL ids.
controls.how: Core has no sessions.
controls.note: Edition concern.

controls.title: Per-ability and per-client authorization on every technician action
controls.requirement: Access control is enforced on the trusted server side, deny by default, least privilege, no object-reference bypass.
controls.how: RmmAuthorizer checks ability and client for every technician action; out-of-scope and missing objects return the same 404.

controls.title: Tenant boundary (client isolation)
controls.requirement: A user limited to some clients cannot read or change another client's objects.
controls.how: CORE-02, CORE-03 and CORE-11 fixes: client visibility and fleet-wide guards on shared objects.
controls.note: CORE-05 (enrollment-token holder can take over a device in the same client) is an open design decision, see GAP-03.

controls.title: CSRF protection
controls.requirement: State-changing requests are protected against cross-site request forgery.
controls.how: Core endpoints authenticate with bearer tokens, not cookies, so ambient-credential CSRF does not apply to them. Cookie-authenticated pages are the edition's.

controls.title: Administrative interfaces are protected
controls.requirement: Admin functions need strong authentication; no directory browsing or leaked metadata.
controls.how: Core's RMM admin actions are gated by abilities (ACC-01); the login in front of them is the edition's.

controls.title: Strict positive validation of agent-supplied identifiers
controls.requirement: Input is validated against an allowlist; trailing-newline bypasses are closed.
controls.how: Exact-match helpers at agent-controlled call sites (CORE-10), schema validation of device payloads and check parameters.
controls.note: The same newline class exists in ~60 other patterns that are not agent-controlled (CORE-10 residual).

controls.title: Parameterized queries
controls.requirement: All database access is parameterized; no string-built SQL from input.
controls.how: Stores use bound parameters; identifiers in dynamic SQL are fixed in code (RetentionService). Enforcement is by review and the audit, not by an automated rule.
controls.note: No static rule forbids concatenated SQL; see GAP-07.

controls.title: SSRF: outbound URLs are vetted and the resolved address is pinned
controls.requirement: Server-side requests to user-supplied URLs are restricted and cannot reach internal hosts.
controls.how: UrlPolicy::vet() resolves, refuses private ranges and odd host spellings, and the dispatcher pins the vetted address.
controls.note: A host that resolves to a public address stays allowed by design. Plain http destinations are accepted (GAP-08).

controls.title: Output encoding and no dynamic code execution
controls.requirement: Output is encoded for its context; no eval, no unsafe deserialization, no shell from input.
controls.how: Core renders no HTML pages of its own except converter output (escaped in DocxConverter) and the shared UI assets. JSON is encoded with fixed flags. No static rule forbids eval, unserialize or shell calls.
controls.note: A grep rule in CI against eval/unserialize/exec in src is cheap; see GAP-07.

controls.title: Log and header injection
controls.requirement: Untrusted data cannot forge log lines or headers.
controls.how: Audit values are clamped and stored as bound data; the HTTP transport rejects control characters in headers (INFO-01).

controls.title: Authenticated encryption with proven primitives
controls.requirement: Approved algorithms, fresh nonces, authenticated modes, constant-time tag check, failures are closed.
controls.how: Envelope: AES-256-GCM through OpenSSL, 96-bit random nonce per call, key id in the envelope, caller AAD bound to the context; fuzzing never opens a damaged value.

controls.title: Key management: random keys, key ids, rotation, rewrap
controls.requirement: Keys come from a CSPRNG, are separable per purpose, and can be rotated without data loss.
controls.how: KeyGenerator uses random_bytes; KeyRing carries several keys; Rewrapper re-seals data under the active key, resumably.
controls.note: Key storage and backup of the key file is the edition's and the operator's (GAP-09: no HSM/KMS integration).

controls.title: Stored credentials are sealed; sensitive objects do not leak through dumps
controls.requirement: Credentials at rest are encrypted; secrets do not appear in debug output, serialization or traces.
controls.how: PostgresConfig, RedisConnectionConfig, SecretString and the VictoriaMetrics store hide secrets from var_dump, (array), serialize and json_encode; sealed passwords are opened only when connecting.
controls.note: var_export of a Redis config still shows the password (CORE-07 residual). Encrypting the edition's own vault rows is the edition's.

controls.title: Signed jobs and update manifests
controls.requirement: Code and jobs sent to agents carry an Ed25519 signature the agent verifies.
controls.how: Signer signs job, check and manifest payloads; known-answer vectors are checked in PHP and Go.
controls.note: INFO-07: no domain-separation prefix on job signatures (frozen protocol, mitigated by field-set validation).

controls.title: Audit trail records security events and is always on
controls.requirement: Authentication, access control and administrative events are logged with who, what, when and from where.
controls.how: AuditService writes actor, entity, action, ip, user agent and request id; the audit_enabled baseline setting is locked on. Core cannot force an edition to call it, and the RMM module logs through AuditServiceRmmAudit.
controls.note: A database failure propagates from AuditService (the caller decides); MCP reads continue if the audit write fails by design.

controls.title: Audit metadata and job output are redacted
controls.requirement: Credentials and tokens never reach logs.
controls.how: AuditService redacts secret-named keys before fan-out and size-caps metadata; Redactor masks job and log output and fails closed on regex errors (CORE-06).
controls.note: The Go agent's own redaction lacks the newer name rules (CORE-18, GAP-05); the server redacts again before storage.

controls.title: Audit retention at least 90 days; changes are audited
controls.requirement: Logs are kept long enough to investigate; the retention setting cannot be set below the floor.
controls.how: SecurityBaseline::auditRetentionDays() (default 365, floor 90) and BaselineChanges (audits accepted and refused changes) enforce the floor at the settings layer. RetentionService::prune() still accepts any horizon unless a compliance profile is passed, so an edition must feed it SecurityBaseline::auditRetentionDays().
controls.note: Making RetentionService itself clamp would change behavior of an existing public class; deferred (GAP-10).

controls.title: Audit log tamper evidence
controls.requirement: Log entries are protected from modification and truncation.
controls.how: Audit rows are plain table rows; there is no hash chain or sealing (INFO-08).
controls.note: GAP-02.

controls.title: Errors fail safe and say little
controls.requirement: Generic error messages, no stack traces to clients, fail closed.
controls.how: ApiError returns coded errors; decryption and validation failures are closed; Redis rate limit fails open on purpose (documented, threat-model section 5).
controls.note: No global last-resort handler in a library; the edition owns it.

controls.title: Clock synchronisation and skew tolerance
controls.requirement: Log time sources are consistent.
controls.how: Database clock is used for retention cutoffs; device check-ins reject skew over 900 s and report it.
controls.note: NTP on servers is operational.

controls.title: Sensitive responses are not cached
controls.requirement: Sensitive responses carry no-store; downloads use attachment disposition and nosniff.
controls.how: RmmResponse JSON sets Cache-Control: no-store; file downloads set nosniff and no-store; panel attachments are served as attachments.

controls.title: Data classification and privacy
controls.requirement: Sensitive data is identified, users can obtain or delete theirs, access is logged.
controls.how: Core does not hold a customer personal-data model beyond device and technician identifiers; export and deletion are the edition's.

controls.title: Backups of the RMM data store are encrypted
controls.requirement: Backup copies of sensitive data are encrypted at rest.
controls.how: scripts/rmm-postgres-backup.sh writes a dump to stdout so the caller encrypts it (documented `| age`); the script itself does not encrypt and defaults sslmode to prefer.
controls.note: GAP-11: no check fails when an unencrypted dump is produced. The edition's own backup (zip or encrypted script) is separate.

controls.title: Restore testing evidence
controls.requirement: Backups are proven restorable.
controls.how: RestoreTestStore records restore tests and compliance checks consume them.
controls.note: Evidence is only as good as the edition feeding it.

controls.title: PostgreSQL: unix socket with peer authentication, or verified TLS
controls.requirement: Connections to the database are local or encrypted with certificate verification.
controls.how: PostgresConfig accepts a socket directory as host (no password needed with peer auth); SecurityBaseline::postgresTransportProblem() reports any remote host below verify-ca. The default sslmode when unset is still prefer, and Core does not refuse a weak configuration; DataStoreSwitch warns (CORE-09).
controls.note: Changing the PostgresConfig default from prefer to verify-full would break existing configs (GAP-01).

controls.title: Redis authentication and TLS support
controls.requirement: Redis supports password/ACL authentication and TLS.
controls.how: RedisConnectionConfig supports password, ACL user and TLS with a timeout; no refusal of an unauthenticated plaintext remote Redis.

controls.title: TLS for inbound traffic and outbound webhooks
controls.requirement: All client connectivity uses TLS 1.2+; HSTS is sent.
controls.how: TLS terminates in the web server of the edition. Core accepts http:// webhook destinations (UrlPolicy allows http and https); the tls_only baseline setting is locked on as the stated rule.
controls.note: GAP-08: Core does not yet refuse plain-http webhook destinations.

controls.title: Security response headers, CSP, CORS
controls.requirement: CSP, Referrer-Policy, frame protection and a strict CORS policy.
controls.how: Core's JSON and download responses set Content-Type, no-store and nosniff. Page-level headers belong to the edition's web layer.

controls.title: Dependencies audited and pinned
controls.requirement: Components are known, current and checked for known vulnerabilities.
controls.how: composer.lock is committed; CI runs composer audit and govulncheck; Dependabot covers composer, actions and Go; CI actions are pinned by commit SHA.
controls.note: No SBOM is published (GAP-12).

controls.title: Release integrity
controls.requirement: Releases are verifiable.
controls.how: Releases carry SHA256SUMS. There is no signature or provenance attestation (INFO-09).
controls.note: GAP-12.

controls.title: Static analysis and secret scanning on every change
controls.requirement: Static analysis runs in the pipeline.
controls.how: PHPStan, lint, our secret scanner (tree and history) and gitleaks run in CI.

controls.title: Enrollment and job flows enforce order and limits
controls.requirement: Business flows cannot be skipped and have sane limits.
controls.how: Enrollment, approval and job states are checked server side; daily budgets and load shedding cap abuse. CORE-05 (reinstall rule) is a documented design weakness.
controls.note: GAP-03.

controls.title: Upload size, type and name checks
controls.requirement: Uploaded files are limited, type-checked, safely named and never executed or rendered inline.
controls.how: PanelAttachments checks format by content, size and count; reserved names refused; served as attachment with nosniff. Converters cap image and document size.
controls.note: INFO-03: crafted OLE upload can inflate memory (admin only, accepted).

controls.title: Antivirus scanning of uploads
controls.requirement: Uploaded files are scanned for malware.
controls.how: No scanner is called.
controls.note: GAP-13.

controls.title: Typed JSON API with content-type and method checks
controls.requirement: APIs validate content type, methods and schema; no secrets in URLs.
controls.how: OpenAPI document for the device API is tested against the routes; requests are parsed into typed objects.
controls.note: Frozen device protocol; not changed by this baseline.

controls.title: MCP tokens: issuer, audience, scope, lifetime
controls.requirement: OAuth bearer tokens are validated for audience, scope and sane lifetime.
controls.how: TokenClaimsGuard requires a dedicated audience, the scope, and a lifetime of at most one hour.

controls.title: Hardened, reviewable build and CI
controls.requirement: Build and deploy pipeline is automated, pinned and reviewable.
controls.how: Workflows run with contents: read, third-party actions pinned by commit, tag-derived input validated (CORE-17), minimal docker and build-host scripts reject symlinked output (CORE-16).

controls.title: Security baseline is itself checked
controls.requirement: The control list cannot rot: referenced files and tests exist, enforced controls have tests, the mapping is current.
controls.how: scripts/baseline-check.php runs in the 'security baseline' CI job and as a unit test.
controls.note: It proves the references exist, not that the tests are good.

controls.title: Vulnerability disclosure policy
controls.requirement: A way to report vulnerabilities and a response commitment.
controls.how: SECURITY.md gives private reporting, acknowledgement in 5 working days, supported versions.

controls.title: Locked-on controls cannot be switched off
controls.requirement: Audit logging, encrypted credentials, TLS-only and Secure/HttpOnly cookies are locked on.
controls.how: SecurityBaseline::SETTINGS marks them locked: validate() refuses false and effective() ignores a stored false. They are rules an edition reads; Core cannot reach into an edition's settings table.

controls.title: Floors are frozen numbers
controls.requirement: Audit retention >= 90 days, password >= 12, session ceiling 480 minutes; changes audit-logged.
controls.how: Constants pinned by test; BaselineChanges audits every accepted and refused change.
controls.note: Applies to callers that go through BaselineChanges; an edition that writes its settings table directly bypasses it.

controls.title: Least-privilege database accounts
controls.requirement: Database roles are non-superuser, own only their database; read-only reporting role.
controls.how: docs/rmm/POSTGRES.md prescribes NOSUPERUSER roles and peer authentication; a separate read-only reporting role reads views only (tested). Core does not create or inspect the production role.
controls.note: Edition installers set up the role (see edition prompts).

controls.title: No default passwords; credentials generated at first use
controls.requirement: Nothing ships with a known password.
controls.how: Core ships no accounts; the signing key and enrollment secrets are minted at enable time; secret scanner blocks committed credentials (AUTH-09).

controls.title: Encrypted backups by default
controls.requirement: Backups are encrypted unless explicitly overridden.
controls.how: See DATA-03; the Core script emits a plain dump for the caller to encrypt.
controls.note: Edition backup tooling must encrypt.

controls.title: Module and remote-tool features are off until enabled
controls.requirement: Unneeded features are disabled by default.
controls.how: The RMM module, enrollment and remote tools refuse until an administrator enables them.

controls.title: Agent state directory permissions
controls.requirement: The agent's config and trusted signing key are not writable by local users.
controls.how: Linux is checked; Windows ownership and reparse points are not (CORE-13, not testable here).
controls.note: GAP-04.

controls.title: Agent job and log redaction
controls.requirement: The Go agent redacts secrets in output before sending.
controls.how: Go redaction exists; newer name rules are server side only (CORE-18).
controls.note: GAP-05.

gaps.title: PostgresConfig default sslmode is prefer
gaps.detail: Changing a public default would break existing configs. The baseline helper reports it; a major version could change it.

gaps.title: CORE-05 enrollment-token reinstall takeover
gaps.detail: Frozen device protocol rule; decision recorded as open.

gaps.title: No static rule against concatenated SQL, eval, unserialize or shell calls
gaps.detail: Cheap to add to CI later.

gaps.title: Plain http webhook destinations are accepted
gaps.detail: UrlPolicy allows http; making it https-only changes behavior.

gaps.title: No KMS/HSM integration for the key file
RetentionService does not clamp the audit horizon itself
gaps.detail: Behavior change on an existing public class.

gaps.title: No check that a produced backup is encrypted
gaps.detail: Script emits a plain dump to stdout.

gaps.title: No SBOM, release signature or provenance attestation
